data.exact_reserve_text: The 2018 pure year result was a modest loss of -0.4%: members benefitted from a gross back year release of GBP 16.1m (GBP 16.1m net of reinsurance, before agency profit commission). A positive run-off of GBP 16.1m on the 2017 and prior years' reserves (2016 and prior: GBP 19.0m) was experienced in the year. This change to the previous closed year reserves was 8.5% of the relevant provisions brought forward.

prior_year_events.impact_description: Syndicate's expected ultimate gross loss across all years of account was revised to $99.4m (prior year $104.0m), with $89.9m incurred at year end; certain legal rulings proved more favourable than initially forecast reducing incurred amounts.
A market-wide arbitration involving a Canadian wildfire reinsurance contract enabled a GBP 3.2m release from reserves.
Better than expected performance on a large Irish motor account (written 2012-16) generated c.60% of a GBP 6.2m gross back-year release.
Syndicate retains modest reserves on the Japanese earthquake and Thai floods of 2010/11 as part of short-tail reserves.
A one-off issue affected 2004, 2014 and prior years; apart from that all earlier years had positive development.

named_events.loss_description: Ultimate gross loss estimate $50.2m, of which $30.8m was incurred at year end; protected by surplus reinsurance and excess of loss covers.
Expected ultimate gross loss across all years of account is now $99.4m (prior year $104.0m), with $89.9m incurred at year end; legal rulings proved more favourable than initially forecast.
Across all 2017 catastrophes project ultimate gross catastrophe losses (after cessions to Syndicate 6103) of $79.2m (prior year $73.7m) with year-end incurred $74.1m.
Included among 2017 catastrophe losses; part of the aggregate catastrophe estimate movements.
Modest reserves retained on Japanese earthquake (2010) and Thai floods (2011) within short-tail account.

data.standardized_narrative: Syndicate 2791 reported a gross release on prior years of GBP 16.1m in the 2020 reporting period (approximately a 5.0% reduction versus opening gross claims outstanding of GBP 322.2m). The release was driven by favourable claims development across both long-tail casualty (c.GBP 5.4m release) and short-tail classes (c.GBP 4.5m), better than expected performance on a large Irish motor account (part of a GBP 6.2m release in auto/specialty classes), and favourable legal/arbitration outcomes (including a GBP 3.2m release from a Canadian wildfire reinsurance arbitration). A small number of older years (notably 2004 and 2014) experienced isolated adverse issues, but overall the movement was a net release.
raw_causal_phrases: members benefitted from a gross back year release of GBP 16.1m (GBP 16.1m net of reinsurance, before agency profit commission).
There was a gross back year release of GBP 16.1m, and the IBNR reserve for 2018 has been set at GBP 17.8m, meaning the ongoing total gross IBNR reserve is now GBP 118.2m.
The long-tail casualty classes generated a GBP 5.4m gross back-year release, and now constitute 40% of the total remaining IBNR reserve (last year 41%).
The short-tail account generated a GBP 4.5m gross back-year release.
There was a GBP 6.2m gross back-year release, 60% of which was generated by a better than expected performance on the large Irish motor account, which we wrote 2012-16.
we prevailed in a market-wide arbitration involving a Canadian wildfire reinsurance contract affecting the 2015 year, which enabled a GBP 3.2m release from reserves.
A positive run-off of GBP 16.1m on the 2017 and prior years' reserves (2016 and prior: GBP 19.0m) was experienced in the year.
data.data_quality_notes: Opening reserves taken from Statement of Financial Position (claims outstanding) comparative column (2019). Prior-year development uses an explicitly stated gross back-year release of GBP 16.1m from the managing agent narrative (gross). Some event loss amounts in the narrative are reported in USD and have not been converted to GBP (left as null). The claims development triangle and technical notes are available but include a RITC relationship with Syndicate 6103 (funds-withheld/quota share) which can distort triangle interpretation; where precise gross movement figures were stated in narrative/notes those were used in preference to triangle-derived calculations.
